# AI Standard

> AI Standard is an independent site for using AI at work. It starts from the task at hand and shows where AI is useful, how to work with it, and what to pay attention to.

Every substantive claim carries an evidence label — Fact, Measured, Law, Assessment or Recommendation — and factual claims carry the date they were last checked against a primary source. Vendor behaviour changes without notice, so a claim here without a date should be treated as unverified.

Available in English at the paths below and in German under `/de/`.

## Start with a question

The three questions the site opens with, each linking to the page that answers it.

- [Can I use AI at work?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/start/employee): What to find out before pasting work material into an AI tool, whom to ask, and what to do when nobody has decided yet.
- [How far does vibe coding take you?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/start/vibe-coding): When leaning on AI generation is enough, what changes once other people depend on the result, and how to tell which stage you are in.
- [How do I connect AI to tools and data?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/connect-ai-to-tools-and-data): When a connection is useful, what it can reach, and how to keep permissions, actions and recovery under control. MCP is the technical example.

## Where AI fits

- [What are you trying to get done?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/use-cases): Six kinds of work, what AI can do for each of them, and where it stops. Deciding to do something without AI is one of the answers.

## Ways of working

- [How do you want to work with AI?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/start): Six ways of working, from asking a question to something that runs without you. What each is good for, and what stays yours in every one of them.
- [Do you need a different tool — or a better setup?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/start/what-it-is-doing): Why a tool problem and a setup problem look alike and are fixed differently, and why how much setup you need does not follow from how skilled you are.
- [I am responsible for AI use by others — where do I start?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/start/decision-maker): Start by finding out what is already in use. Then the AI literacy duty under AI Act Art. 4, what to decide first, and why banning tools produces shadow IT.

## Access & actions

- [What can it access, and what can it do?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows): Four things worth separating when an AI system is connected to something: what it can read, what stays stored, what it can change, and what it can set off elsewhere.
- [Are your chats used for model training?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/training-and-retention): Training depends on the product, the account type and the settings, not on the vendor. Includes the trap of a developer tool on a personal account.
- [What changes when you allow model training](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/what-you-agree-to): At some providers one setting governs both training and how long conversations are kept.
- [Deleting chats and data: what goes and what stays](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/getting-it-back-out): What deleting a chat actually removes, which deletion duties exist, and why getting a copy out is a separate question from deleting one.
- [Where your data is, and who can reach it](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/data-sovereignty): The operating models, the axes they differ on, and what a hosting location does not tell you.
- [Which of your systems can be a knowledge source](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/data-flows/where-knowledge-lives): Why mail is a poor place to keep what you know, and what each kind of system is good at.

## Secure & verify

- [How do you set limits that hold — and check what happened?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/secure-setup): How much checking a task needs follows from the consequence of a mistake, not from the tool. What to settle first, how a boundary holds, what to check, and what to keep.
- [Before you give an AI agent access](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/secure-setup/before-you-grant-access): What to decide before an agent gets a folder, why a boundary has to be enforced outside the model, what a useful approval shows, and how to take an access back.
- [Checking the result](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/secure-setup/checking-the-result): How to check what an AI system produced and what it did — proportionate to the consequence, and different for an answer, a change and an action.
- [Keeping a record](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/secure-setup/keeping-a-record): Why a chat history is not a record of a decision, the four things worth writing down when AI did part of the work, and where they belong.

## Law

The legal questions that come up when you use AI at work: what may be entered, confidentiality and data protection, transfers outside the EU, and the AI Act's own duties.

- [Which rules apply when you use AI at work?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/law): The four legal questions, and which page answers each of them.
- [Which legal question are you asking?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/law/four-separate-questions): Data protection, AI regulation, confidentiality and security test different things — different answers, different sources.
- [Can I enter this data into an AI tool?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/law/what-may-go-in): Personal data and confidentiality are two questions with two different answers. Includes the six legal bases under Art. 6 GDPR and why consent is rarely the one at work.
- [Does a US-hosted AI tool break the GDPR?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/law/us-cloud-and-the-gdpr): "It runs in the US, so it is illegal" is not what the regulation says — and "it runs in the EU" is not compliance.
- [AI Act: labelling AI-generated content](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/law/ai-act-transparency): Article 50 has applied since 2 August 2026. What must be disclosed, who is obliged, and what the transition covers.

## Open source

Questions that arrive once software — including software built with AI — is published or maintained: the licence, the obligations, and who holds the rights.

- [Open source](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/open-source): What makes a project open source, which licence commits you to what, and who owns code written at work.
- [When is a project open source?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/open-source/what-makes-it-open-source): The licence decides, not visibility. Includes what GitHub's own terms permit without one.
- [Which licence, and what does it commit you to?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/open-source/choosing-a-licence): Permissive, file-level copyleft, strong copyleft — and what the adoption numbers do and do not support.
- [Who owns code written at work?](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/open-source/code-written-at-work): § 40b Austrian and § 69b German Copyright Act give rights of use, not authorship. US work-for-hire is a different construction, and AI-written portions raise a further question about what a licence can grant.

## Glossary

- [Glossary](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/glossary): AI, data protection and tooling terms, with the confusable ones paired.

## About

- [About AI Standard](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/about): Why this site exists, the position it argues from, what it is not, and who writes it.
- [How claims are checked](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/about/how-claims-are-checked): What each claim label means, what has to be true before a claim is published under it, how sources are ranked, and what to do when something here is wrong.
- [Blog](https://ai-standard.rubennati.at/blog): Authored, dated pieces that follow one question far enough to be worth reading.
